name: GMX v1 GLP reentrancy short-price manipulation
summary: PositionManager.executeDecreaseOrder wraps order execution in enableLeverage/disableLeverage and refunds native ETH to the order account, which can be a contract; the refund re-enters mid-flow while leverage is enabled, letting the attacker open Vault shorts that drive shortsTracker.globalShortAveragePrices far below spot. GlpManager.getAum prices GLP from that reentrancy-manipulable global-short average with no manipulation resistance, so GLP minted before and redeemed after the manipulation over-withdraws the Vault's reserves.

loss.notes: The measured loss is the net decrease of the GMX Vault's nine external reserve assets during the drain transaction 0x03182d3f (source-2), 274 seconds after the anchor. Per-asset net = Vault Transfer-out minus Transfer-in in that receipt: USDC out 18,291,966,230,478 minus in 8,538,567,619,570 = 9,753,398,610,908 base units; FRAX out 28,958,626,304,231,692,487,914,531 minus in 18,410,000,000,000,000,000,000,000 = 10,548,626,304,231,692,487,914,531; the other seven assets have no same-transaction Vault inflow. The attacker's own staked GLP token (0x45096e7a, fsGLP) transfers in and out of the Vault in equal amount (67,266,389,486,834,066,844,513,960) and nets to zero, so it is excluded. The earlier anchor rehearsal 0x1f00d added 3,001 USDC to the Vault and withdrew 0.009963368148593124 WETH, a net gain to the Vault, so it contributes no victim loss and is not netted against the drain. Volatile assets (WBTC, WETH, LINK, UNI) use DefiLlama historical prices within ten seconds before the drain; the five stable assets use par. The attacker later returned roughly 40.5M of the proceeds to GMX under a 10% white-hat bounty settlement; per methodology that recovery does not reduce gross victim depletion and is not netted here.

ageReset.description: PositionManager is a direct, non-proxy contract (EIP-1967 implementation slot zero, no code change). The reentrancy is inherent to executeDecreaseOrder wrapping the order in enableLeverage/disableLeverage and refunding native ETH to an arbitrary account; no parameter value makes the deployed code correct, so deployment is the age basis. Its runtime hash is byte-identical at the creation block and immediately before the anchor.

GlpManager is a direct, non-proxy contract (EIP-1967 implementation slot zero, no code change). getAum/getGlobalShortAveragePrice price GLP from a live global-short average price that can be manipulated within one transaction via reentrant short opens. The shortsTrackerAveragePriceWeight parameter (10000 at exploit time, selecting shortsTracker.globalShortAveragePrices) only chooses which manipulable average is read; vault.globalShortAveragePrices is equally reentrancy-manipulable, so no parameter value removes the defect and deployment is the age basis. Runtime hash is byte-identical at the creation block and immediately before the anchor.

sources.note: Independently reproduced the anchor, the drain and both targets on Arbitrum. Attacker EOA 0xdf3340...a5221 deployed the attack contract 0x7d3bd5...cc355 at nonce 1 (block 355876960), created an increase order at nonce 3 (0x0b8cd, block 355878385) and a decrease order at nonce 4 (0x20abf, block 355878984). GMX's keeper 0xd4266f...160f3 then executed executeIncreaseOrder (0x28a00, block 355878605) and executeDecreaseOrder twice: 0x1f00d (block 355879148, index 12, the anchor) and 0x03182 (block 355880237, index 2, the drain). callTracer on 0x28a00 shows zero calls into the attack contract, so the increase execution does not re-enter; 0x1f00d is the earliest successful transaction that exercises the reentrancy defect. In 0x1f00d, PositionManager.executeDecreaseOrder calls Timelock.enableLeverage (0x6d63c1d0), then OrderBook.executeDecreaseOrder decreases the position via Vault, unwraps WETH and sends 0.009963368148593124 ETH to the attack contract; the attack contract's receive re-enters while leverage is enabled, reading GlpManager.getGlobalShortAveragePrice (0x440d828a -> shortsTracker) and Vault prices and performing Vault/Router operations before the outer flow and disableLeverage complete. shortsTrackerAveragePriceWeight = 10000 and isGlobalShortDataReady = true pre-exploit, so GlpManager.getAum reads shortsTracker.globalShortAveragePrices, whose WBTC value was 108,757.787 (1e30 precision) before the attack. In the drain 0x03182, GlpManager emits 4 AddLiquidity and 11 RemoveLiquidity events: the attacker mints GLP cheaply and, after driving the global short average price down, redeems GLP at inflated AUM, over-withdrawing the Vault. Loss = the net Vault depletion of nine external reserve assets in the 0x03182 receipt, computed from Transfer logs into/out of the Vault: WBTC 88.17336478, WETH 3205.50915468372143587, USDC.e 187343.427631, LINK 23800.209308406681099727, UNI 65479.241421767977905495, USDT 1343601.991557, FRAX 10548626.304231692487914531 (out 28,958,626.30... minus in 18,410,000 recycled), DAI 1338385.137937366936342579, USDC 9753398.610908 (out 18,291,966.23... minus in 8,538,567.62 recycled); staked GLP fsGLP 0x45096e7a nets to zero and is excluded. Volatile assets valued at DefiLlama historical prices within 10 s before the drain (WBTC 109430, WETH 2658.32, LINK 14.13, UNI 8.18); stables at par; total 42,213,353.03 USD. Target identity/age: PositionManager 0x75e42e...4a0c top-level created by GMX deployer 0x5f799f...0cf8 in 0xcd5b472c at block 29852256 index 1 timestamp 1665653281; GlpManager 0x3963ff...ec18 created by the same deployer in 0x41cae530 at block 40559781 index 1 timestamp 1669211116. Both are direct non-proxy contracts: EIP-1967 implementation slot reads zero at block 355879147, and each contract's eth_getCode runtime hashes identically at its creation block and immediately before the anchor (PositionManager 0xf9175761...05e57, GlpManager 0x830f5253...a1eeb), so neither executable code changed. Verified BscScan/Arbiscan-style verified sources for GlpManager (getAum, getGlobalShortAveragePrice, addLiquidity, removeLiquidity) and PositionManager. No parameter value removes either defect (the reentrancy window is inherent; both the shortsTracker and vault short-average stores are reentrancy-manipulable), so deployment is the age basis for both. Code age at the anchor: PositionManager 86,410,656 s (about 2.74 years), GlpManager 82,852,821 s (about 2.63 years). Attacker addresses are the EOA and its attack contract; the GMX keeper is excluded. Mechanism cross-checked against Verichains' root-cause analysis (source-7).

notes: Anchored to the earliest successful keeper executeDecreaseOrder that triggers the attacker's reentrant callback (0x1f00d, block 355879148), 274 seconds before the large drain 0x03182 (block 355880237). The keeper 0xd4266f...160f3 is GMX's own order-execution keeper, not an attacker address; it unwittingly executes the attacker-created order and delivers the reentrant ETH refund. This supersedes an earlier draft that anchored on the drain transaction.

The Vault (0x489ee0...97c4a), ShortsTracker (0xf58eec83...434da), OrderBook (0x09f77e8a...2acb), Timelock (0x5cf5e6a4...15f42) and Router (0xabbc5f99...4064) are exercised in the trace but are not independently defect-bearing: the Vault correctly gates increasePosition on leverage being enabled, ShortsTracker records the averages it is fed, and the others are routing. The two defect-bearing roles are the reentrancy window (PositionManager) and the reentrancy-manipulable GLP pricing (GlpManager).
